title: There is no FLASH_ACR_LATENCY_1 for STM32C0 devices
body:
Hi everyone 👋

The FLASH Latency (LATENCY[2:0] in FLASH_ACR) can be either one or two wait states (`0b000` or `0b001`; see RM0490 Rev 5, Chapter 4.3.2 or 4.7.1). Therefore, only bit 0 is available in C0 devices. 

I suggest deleting the macro definition for FLASH_ACR_LATENCY_1 e.g.: [stm32c011xx.h](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-c0/blob/517611273f835ffe95318947647bc1408f69120d/Include/stm32c011xx.h#L2273C1-L2273C102) from all device header files to avoid confusions - because I got confused myself 😅. In other devices, only the usable bits are defined as well.

Best Simon

comments.author: TOUNSTM
comments.body:
Hello @slpuls,

Thank you for your feedback. The CMSIS header files are intended to provide a direct and accurate representation of the hardware registers, as specified in the reference manual. Therefore, if the reference manual indicates that the LATENCY field is 3 bits wide (LATENCY[2:0]), the CMSIS headers will define the mask and bit positions for all three bits, even if not all possible values are currently supported by the device. On the other hand, the HAL drivers are designed to expose only the valid and supported latency values for your specific device, such as:
```
#define FLASH_LATENCY_0                 0x00000000UL                /*!< FLASH Zero wait state */
#define FLASH_LATENCY_1                 FLASH_ACR_LATENCY_0         /*!< FLASH One wait state */
```
I hope this explanation clarifies any confusion. If you have any further questions or need additional information, please feel free to ask.

Best regards,

comments.author: slpuls
comments.body: Thanks for your answer, then the macro definition for FLASH_ACR_LATENCY_2 is missing in all device header files.

comments.author: TOUNSTM
comments.body:
Hello @slpuls,

Thank you for highlighting this point. After consulting with our development team, we confirm that your observation is correct: typically, reserved values are not provided in the CMSIS headers. However, to maintain backward compatibility and avoid any potential regressions for existing customers, we have decided to retain the FLASH_ACR_LATENCY_1 definition.

We appreciate your understanding. Please allow me to close this issue.

Kind regards,

title: Initial value of SystemCoreClock incorrect
body:
`SystemCoreClock` is currently defined in system_stm32c0xx.c [like this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_c0/blob/v1.1.0/Source/Templates/system_stm32c0xx.c#L110):

```c
  uint32_t SystemCoreClock = 48000000UL;
```

The variable `SystemCoreClock` holds the system core clock, which is the system clock frequency supplied to the processor core clock (see [here](https://arm-software.github.io/CMSIS_5/Core/html/group__system__init__gr.html#gae0c36a9591fe6e9c45ecb21a794f0f0f).)

On the STM32C0, HSISYS is used as system clock source after startup from reset, with a division factor of four. This results in a system clock frequency of 12 MHz being supplied to the processor core clock.

In my opinion, the current definition of `SystemCoreClock` is incorrect and it should be defined as like this:

```c
  uint32_t SystemCoreClock = 12000000UL;
```
